topic: AI will create more jobs than it cuts, but 11M Americans may need new careers
post:
AI will create more jobs than it cuts. 📈
That's the good news. Here's the part that matters for your career.

A new McKinsey Global Institute report estimates that by 2035 in the U.S.:

➖ AI and automation cut demand for about 36 million jobs
➕ Growth elsewhere creates about 41 million jobs
🔄 But about 11 million workers, roughly 7% of the workforce, may need to change occupations entirely

The catch: only about 1 in 7 displaced workers has a direct path to a growing job.

McKinsey's own summary: "The next decade's challenge is mobility, not scarcity."

Why it matters:
The risk isn't that work disappears. It's being stuck in a shrinking role without a bridge to a growing one.

Practical takeaway for this week:
1️⃣ List the 3 tasks in your job AI could do soonest
2️⃣ List the 3 tasks only you can do (judgment, relationships, context)
3️⃣ Spend one hour building a skill that grows list #2

Your bridge to the next role starts with that second list.

What's one skill you're building to stay ahead? 👇
